newsitem.title: USA: N.J. unemployment rate rises to 5.3 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: N.J. unemployment rate rises to 5.3 pct in May.

text.p: New Jersey's seasonally-adjusted unemployment rate rose to 5.3 percent in May from 5.2 percent in April, the state's Department of Labor said Friday.
The figure is down 0.8 of a percentage point from the May 1996 rate of 6.1 percent.
The number of jobs rose 3,100 in May, bringing non-farm payrolls in the state to nearly 3.7 million.

"New Jersey's economy is performing well," New Jersey Labor Commissioner Mel Gelade said in a statement. "Ongoing job growth has raised employment to its highest level since September 1989 and our unemployment rate is nearly a percentage point lower than where it stood at this time last year."
Job growth was highest in the services division, up 4,700 from April to May.
Following a downturn of 600 jobs in April, construction employment rebounded by 700 in May to a seasonally-adjusted level of 126,400.
Manufacturing employment fell by 2,600 from April to May, with the biggest declines coming in electronic equipment and food processing, which fell by 600 jobs each.
